Marissa / Kim — thanks for the flag. Quick legal/contract position below (high level) and attached redline for SCCs: SCCs_draft_redline.docx.

Legal position (short bullets):
- We can accept the EU SCCs for hosted customers; we propose the standard insertion clarifying processing roles and subprocessor list references. No blanket refusal.
- For customers requiring dedicated capacity or on-prem, we recommend using our DPA annex + Appendix A (data flows) rather than SCCs.
- BYOK: supported. For BYOK customers we include explicit key custody clause and limited access controls; BYOK customers assume responsibility for key rotation.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (GCP/Azure) and HSM-backed keys via partner HSM offerings — see kms_key_management_summary.txt.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache does not persist customer PII beyond defined TTLs; caching is per-tenant when on Dedicated EU pools. For shared-hosted routing, we recommend enabling tenant-scoped prefix caching and retention controls; add wording to DPA annex.

I’ve annotated the Bluehaven questions in the attached and included a redline for SCCs that: 1) limits subprocessor delegation language, 2) clarifies remedies for export law conflicts, and 3) adds a data flow appendix reference.

-Karthik
